scenes.narration: Normally every router reads the full destination address. It does that at every single hop, which is slow. M P L S puts a short label on instead.

scenes.heading: Express train labels
scenes.narration: Think of a parcel sorting network. Normally every sorting centre reads the whole address. M P L S sticks a short label on at the first centre. Each centre in the middle just swaps the label and passes it on. The last centre removes the label and delivers it.

scenes.heading: Facts to remember
scenes.narration: A few details show up on the exam. M P L S sits between layer two and layer three. A label is thirty two bits long. The three actions are push, swap and pop. L D P shares labels on port six four six.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three mix-ups. Only the first router looks up the I P address. The label is pushed on at the ingress router. And penultimate hop popping means the second last router removes the label.

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.narration: So, to recap. M P L S forwards on short labels instead of full addresses. The actions are push, swap and pop. It sits at layer two and a half. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva MPLS lab.

points.t: Forwards on labels, not full IPs
